units.text: INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S KITCHEN - NIGHT
A round room, whitewashed.
A kettle ticks on an iron stove.
Rain slides down the glass in slow threads.
Five places are set at a table built for four.
GRANDMOTHER ILONA (80s, shawl, hands folded) watches the empty fifth chair.
Her grandson TOBY (20s, damp jacket) stirs his soup and does not drink it.
His wife NELL (20s, pregnant, cardigan buttoned wrong) counts the spoons.
NELL'S BROTHER RAFE (30s, unshaven) pours whisky into his tea.
And the housekeeper, MRS. PATTERSON (60s, apron), sets down bread with exaggerated care.
The lamp above the table dims.
Brightens.
Toby, the bread.
units.name: GRANDMOTHER ILONA

units.text: Thank you, Gran.
units.name: TOBY

units.text: He doesn't take any.
Nell slides the board toward him with one finger.
Rafe, you were out at the rocks today.
units.name: NELL

units.text: Checking the lines.
units.name: RAFE

units.text: Find anything?
units.name: NELL

units.text: Nothing worth mentioning, Nell.
units.name: RAFE

units.text: Mrs. Patterson sets a sixth bowl at the fifth place.
Nobody comments.
The kettle goes quiet.
The soup steams across the empty chair.
Mrs. Patterson, thank you.
units.name: GRANDMOTHER ILONA

units.text: He always liked the leeks.
units.name: MRS. PATTERSON

units.text: Toby puts down his spoon.
Rafe turns his cup in a slow circle.
Far above them, the great lamp grinds round, and its beam crosses the window once, white, then gone.
